summary.en: Pakistan has kept the Zangali and Torkham Iran crossings closed, creating a backlog of 2,271 trucks, while only limited trade has resumed under partial operations. The closure has driven an unprecedented rise in LPG prices, which the Pakistani minister attributes to the border shutdown, and the government has launched an operation against illegal Afghans in Peshawar and banned gatherings in Balochistan's Pishin ahead of an intensified campaign. Pakistan accuses the Taliban of using Afghan territory to launch attacks against it, while the Taliban government has reshuffled civilian and military officials in Badakhshan. The conflict recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistan har holdt grenseovergangene Zangali og Torkham mot Iran stengt, noe som har ført til en kø på 2 271 lastebiler, mens kun begrenset handel har gjenopptatt under delvis drift. Stengingen har ført til en enestående økning i LPG-prisene, som den pakistanske ministeren tilskriver grenselukket, og regjeringen har igangsatt en operasjon mot ulovlige afghanere i Peshawar og forbudt forsamlinger i Balochistans Pishin i forkant av en skjerpet kampanje. Pakistan anklager Taliban for å bruke afghansk territorium til å gjennomføre angrep mot landet, mens Taliban-regjeringen har gjort om på sivile og militære tjenestemenn i Badakhshan. Konflikten registrerte 1 794 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
